A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WildScore and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Their methods, results, tables and figures can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, human-expert performance, perception diagnostics, ABC reconstruction findings and an appendix bias check.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including model accuracies in Tables 3–5 and reconstruction and bias-check findings in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure remains unchanged: YOLO filtering, GPT-assisted MCQ creation, engagement-based answer selection, model tie-breaking and distractor generation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 807-item Reddit-derived benchmark, five categories and twelve subcategories. Image-plus-text, text-only, perception and score-reconstruction tasks are retained without additional coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 evaluate the same seven MLLMs. The human-expert comparison and Appendix D comparison between GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1-mini are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The modality conditions, accuracy metric and reported model sizes are unchanged. Both retain the 100-question human evaluation, 50-image perception probe and 50-item bias-check subset.

E4.justification: Image-removal comparisons, category analyses, perception diagnostics, ABC reconstruction analysis and the judge/formatting bias check already appear in v1 and are retained in v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. GPT-4.1-mini retains 68.31% accuracy with images and 65.76% without; Appendix D retains 58% for GPT-4.1 versus 50% for GPT-4.1-mini. Table 8's reconstruction findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The scoring rule S = U − D and stated definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The claims concerning the first in-the-wild symbolic music reasoning benchmark, its taxonomy, MCQ formulation and model limitations retain the same scope. The abstract's wording adjustment does not change its scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model-dependent image benefits, perception versus reasoning failures, and text-only performance are retained. The discussion of Reddit sampling biases and content limitations is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Construction details, model sizes, Appendix A prompts and Appendix C annotator instructions are retained. Dataset and code links and licensing information are unchanged; the corrected appendix reference only improves navigation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Surana et al. (2022) to the introduction. It also changes MusicScore's citation from Chou et al. (2023) to Lin et al. (2024) in Section 2.1, Table 1 and the bibliography. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 fixes wording and typographical errors, changes the Section 3.4 appendix reference from 5 to C, removes the misplaced Human Annotation Details heading before Diagnostic 2, and renumbers the conclusion. It also adds an NSF funding acknowledgment.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned, notably Tables 3–4 from PDF page 7 to page 8. Table 8 receives revised rules, spacing and text wrapping. All five figures and nine tables are retained, with unchanged figure content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by correcting the Appendix C reference and removing the misleading heading that interrupted the error analysis. Typo fixes and cleaner Table 8 formatting also improve readability. The scientific evidence, reproducibility information and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
